input: the findings of Claude Code review and Codex review in h2h/findings_claude.json and h2h/findings_codex.json

bugs.claim: _run_models_sync only catches RuntimeError, so an OSError/PermissionError from the lock or write in sync_starter_registry (e.g. unwritable registry directory with --apply) escapes as a traceback instead of 'error: ...' and exit 1.

On the BaseException path (e.g. KeyboardInterrupt in communicate) _run_cli kills the process group but never waits on the Popen or closes its pipes, so the child stays unreaped (returncode None) and pipes stay open, unlike subprocess.run.

The hint looks up the starter entry by exact id only. When the registry holds the same adapter/model under another id (cursor/my-grok, disabled), it says the entry is absent and advises `models sync --apply`, which plan_starter_sync skips as covered.

_run_models_sync catches only RuntimeError, so with --apply on a registry in a non-writable directory the lock acquisition raises PermissionError and the CLI crashes with a traceback instead of printing 'error: ...' and returning 1.

The lookup is by exact id only, so a disabled entry with the same adapter and model under another id (cursor/my-grok) is reported as absent and the user is told to run `models sync --apply`, which skips it as covered.

The hint text has no registry path and the function takes none, so for a task with a custom registry_path the suggested `models sync --apply` and enable commands omit --registry-path and act on the default registry.
